page: Amazon Web Services p5en.48xlarge is an accelerated computing instance engineered for massive deep learning and high-performance computing clusters. Operated via the AWS Nitro hypervisor, the platform pairs an Intel x86_64 host processor with eight NVIDIA Hopper H200 graphics processing units. The CPU architecture provides 192 dedicated virtual CPUs across 96 physical cores running at a clock frequency of 2.4 GHz. Host system memory totals 2048 GB, yielding 10.67 GB per physical core. The eight attached H200 GPUs deliver a combined total of 1128 GB of high-bandwidth accelerator memory.

The instance integrates substantial on-box storage and network capacity. Local storage is supplied via 30400 GB of bundled NVMe SSD capacity, allowing massive training datasets to reside directly on the node to accelerate data ingestion pipelines without recurring transfer overhead. For inter-node synchronization, the server provides a baseline network throughput of 3200 Gbps. This bandwidth is designed to sustain collective communication patterns such as all-reduce operations across multi-node clusters, preventing network bottlenecks during distributed execution.

From an operational standpoint, the dense resource profile aggregates accelerator compute, high-capacity local NVMe storage, and multi-terabit networking into a single machine, reducing cluster node counts for large workloads. The primary operational tradeoff centers on maintaining near-continuous utilization of its high-density hardware to realize its throughput advantages. This instance is best aligned with large language model pre-training, multi-node distributed fine-tuning, high-throughput transformer inference, and large-scale scientific modeling.

Host system resources include 2048 GB of RAM, yielding 10.67 GB per physical core, complemented by 30400 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage.
